The Aboriginal Nation - a Khoi-san Scam

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight we show how people are being scammed into giving money to a so-called Khoisan Empress and her henchmen and women

Unique Selling Point:
This is an exclusive dive into a movement aimed at reviving the heritage of the Khoi and San which appears to have been hijacked by people interested in making money off poor coloured people. We join the dots to explain how the Khoisan ID came to South Africa and how people are manipulating a sense of identity to give people false hope of great wealth

Summary:
In following up the story of the Khoisan ID allegedly provided to MK for padding their lists of signatures to get on to the ballot, I have stumbled upon a number of Khoisan Identity Scams where people claiming to lead the Khoisan target and exploit working class coloured people. It’s a hornet nest of competing interests.

In particular, a Khoisan Grouping who have organised themselves around Queen Valerie Sabina Letsie 111, who they claim is an Empress of all Indigenous/Khoisan people, and her Ambassador, one Edgar Adams. They target people who they describe as so-called coloureds and help them believe that they are Khoisan/Aboriginals/First People and have the right to own all the wealth of South Africa. They have collected devotees through word of mouth and persuaded them through a whatsapp group to first pay for their Khoisan ID (which has not materialised) and also pool funds to start an Aboriginal Bank which will create wealth for all those with IDs.

Through crude propaganda and a mixture of evangelical religion, they groom their followers and encourage them to donate. The admins of the whatsapp group delete all negative comments. They publish the amounts saved on the whatsapp group. In a few weeks they raised about R80k for their devotees, many of whom claim to be poor and battling to afford the R100. They have written a song that refutes their coloured status and reclaims them as an Aboriginal nation

Queen Valerie Sabina Letsie 111 and her followers including her three handmaidens are marching on Parliament on the 30th of July which is Tuesday. She is actually from Durban and is in a wheelchair.

They are in fact a splinter group off another Khoisan grouping led by so-called Dr Gregg Fick, who had been holding workshops around the country getting people to sign up for a Khoisan IDs, on the premises that they might get a part of a mult-million rand pay out in the Equality Court. He called his Group First Indigenous Nation of Southern Africa (FINSA). Fick is at war with an MK MP who calls himself is Kai Bi’a Glen Taaibosch, King of the Kei! who worked with him originally, but then apparently stole his Aboriginal ID database and gave it to Zuma to get on to the ballot paper. Taaibosch was working with Fick before he split and sided with Zuma. He calls his organisation F

If this is sounding a bit crazy, it is.

I have been sitting in the whatsapp group of the Empress Letsie the 111 since the elections. I have spent two hours with Gregg Fick, but he is not that keen to go on camera. However, he is eloquently on Facebook, and took time to rebut our Carte Blanche piece on Facebook.

The crux of the story is that conmen and women are exploiting a sense of identity insecurity to persuade people to first hand over their personal details and secondly hand over cash, promising them future wealth which will not materialise. It’s a hoax.


Further information:
Background on the Law

Secondly, this jostling for power within a community with Khoisan heritage is to some degree as a result of a law which was passed in 2019 called the Traditional and Khoisan Leadership Act which attempts to bring the Khoisan traditional leadership into line with the traditional leaders – that is provide them with recognition and perks.

This had led to a scramble for positions. According to the law, a person applying to be a senior Khoisan leader of a community needs to have a list of all community members with full name, surnames and valid certified identification document. There are complex procedures to allow for people to be Kings, Queens and headmen or women, but it involves the state, essentially politicising the process, partly because a provincial premier can withdraw the recognition of that person who claims to be royal. Further resources from the state may be made available to them at the Minister’s discretion.

The law was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court in May 2023 because it would result in abuse of the very people it is meant to recognise. The court suspended the act for 24 months to facilitate a constitutional complaint process so it’s back on the drawing board.

Press Release:


Aboriginal Nation
A self-styled indigenous empress poised to pay out billions of rands hidden in a secret trust to the descendants of the Khoi and San in South Africa: if only it were true. But it’s not, despite what the imperial leaders have told a vast network of WhatsApp groups where they groom poor people to pledge their scarce cash to the scheme. They say the ticket to great wealth is an Aboriginal ID, purchased online. This card will supposedly help beneficiaries cash in, and give them immunity to South African law. This scam is part of a larger movement to create a Khoisan leadership class worthy of state perks and influence. We penetrate the campaign of Empress Valerie Sabina Letsie III who revealed herself in front of Parliament this week, and identify two more groups that have taken cash from people desperate to get a cut of the multi-million rand payout that’s promised in the name of their Khoisan legacy.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles

I have been sitting in the whatsapp group of the Empress Letsie the 111 since the elections. I have spent two hours with Gregg Fick, but he is not that keen to go on camera. However, he is eloquently on Facebook, and took time to rebut our Carte Blanche piece on Facebook. The crux of the story is that conmen and women are exploiting a sense of identity insecurity to persuade people to first hand over their personal details and secondly hand over cash, promising them future wealth which will not materialise. It’s a hoax. Further information: Background on the Law Secondly, this jostling for power within a community with Khoisan heritage is to some degree as a result of a law which was passed in 2019 called the Traditional and Khoisan Leadership Act which attempts to bring the Khoisan traditional leadership into line with the traditional leaders – that is provide them with recognition and perks. This had led to a scramble for positions. According to the law, a person applying to be a senior Khoisan leader of a community needs to have a list of all community members with full name, surnames and valid certified identification document. There are complex procedures to allow for people to be Kings, Queens and headmen or women, but it involves the state, essentially politicising the process, partly because a provincial premier can withdraw the recognition of that person who claims to be royal. Further resources from the state may be made available to them at the Minister’s discretion. The law was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court in May 2023 because it would result in abuse of the very people it is meant to recognise. The court suspended the act for 24 months to facilitate a constitutional complaint process so it’s back on the drawing board. empress poised to pay out billions of rands hidden in a secret trust to the descendants of the Khoi and San in South Africa: if only it were true. But it’s not, despite what the imperial leaders have told a vast network of WhatsApp groups where they groom poor people to pledge their scarce cash to the scheme. They say the ticket to great wealth is an Aboriginal ID, purchased online. This card will supposedly help beneficiaries cash in, and give them immunity to South African law. This scam is part of a larger movement to create a Khoisan leadership class worthy of state perks and influence. We penetrate the campaign of Empress Valerie Sabina Letsie III who revealed herself in front of Parliament this week, and identify two more groups that have taken cash from people desperate to get a cut of the multi-million rand payout that’s promised in the name of their Khoisan legacy. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight we show how people are being scammed into giving money to a so-called Khoisan Empress and her henchmen and women
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is an exclusive dive into a movement aimed at reviving the heritage of the Khoi and San which appears to have been hijacked by people interested in making money off poor coloured people. We join the dots to explain how the Khoisan ID came to South Africa and how people are manipulating a sense of identity to give people false hope of great wealth
metadata.Summary: In following up the story of the Khoisan ID allegedly provided to MK for padding their lists of signatures to get on to the ballot, I have stumbled upon a number of Khoisan Identity Scams where people claiming to lead the Khoisan target and exploit working class coloured people. It’s a hornet nest of competing interests. In particular, a Khoisan Grouping who have organised themselves around Queen Valerie Sabina Letsie 111, who they claim is an Empress of all Indigenous/Khoisan people, and her Ambassador, one Edgar Adams. They target people who they describe as so-called coloureds and help them believe that they are Khoisan/Aboriginals/First People and have the right to own all the wealth of South Africa. They have collected devotees through word of mouth and persuaded them through a whatsapp group to first pay for their Khoisan ID (which has not materialised) and also pool funds to start an Aboriginal Bank which will create wealth for all those with IDs. Through crude propaganda and a mixture of evangelical religion, they groom their followers and encourage them to donate. The admins of the whatsapp group delete all negative comments. They publish the amounts saved on the whatsapp group. In a few weeks they raised about R80k for their devotees, many of whom claim to be poor and battling to afford the R100. They have written a song that refutes their coloured status and reclaims them as an Aboriginal nation Queen Valerie Sabina Letsie 111 and her followers including her three handmaidens are marching on Parliament on the 30th of July which is Tuesday. She is actually from Durban and is in a wheelchair. They are in fact a splinter group off another Khoisan grouping led by so-called Dr Gregg Fick, who had been holding workshops around the country getting people to sign up for a Khoisan IDs, on the premises that they might get a part of a mult-million rand pay out in the Equality Court. He called his Group First Indigenous Nation of Southern Africa (FINSA). Fick is at war with an MK MP who calls himself is Kai Bi’a Glen Taaibosch, King of the Kei! who worked with him originally, but then apparently stole his Aboriginal ID database and gave it to Zuma to get on to the ballot paper. Taaibosch was working with Fick before he split and sided with Zuma. He calls his organisation F If this is sounding a bit crazy, it is. I have been sitting in the whatsapp group of the Empress Letsie the 111 since the elections. I have spent two hours with Gregg Fick, but he is not that keen to go on camera. However, he is eloquently on Facebook, and took time to rebut our Carte Blanche piece on Facebook. The crux of the story is that conmen and women are exploiting a sense of identity insecurity to persuade people to first hand over their personal details and secondly hand over cash, promising them future wealth which will not materialise. It’s a hoax.
